title: Major depression: episode, severity and remission
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's depressive disorder.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for depression.

HPI: Patient is an 81-year-old female with a history of major depressive disorder, recurrent. She was seen previously for management of depressive symptoms and has been adhering to her prescribed regimen. She reports stable mood and consistent energy levels since the last evaluation. 

Update: Today, the patient reports feeling very well. She denies any feelings of hopelessness or significant changes in sleep or appetite. She states she feels she has returned to her baseline functioning.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F.

Review of Systems:
Neuro: Negative
Psych: Negative
CV: Negative
Resp: Negative
GI: Negative
MSK: Negative

Medication List:
Sertraline 50mg daily

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3. Well-groomed and cooperative.
Mood: Euthymic.
Affect: Full and congruent.
Speech: Normal rate and volume.
Thought Process: Linear and goal-directed.

Assessment:
1. Major depressive disorder, recurrent. The patient is currently in full remission.

Plan:
1. Continue current medication.
2. Follow up in 3 months for routine monitoring.

Electronically signed, J. Lindqvist, MD
05/14/2026
explanations: Major depressive disorder, recurrent, in full remission (no HCC): F33.42.

distractors.why: The provider documents full remission: code the remission, not an active severity.
The remission is full, not partial.
